q: The Log-rank conjecture in communication complexity states that the deterministic communication complexity D(f) is polynomially related to the log of the rank of the communication matrix M_f:
opts: D(f) = O(log rank(M_f)^c) for some constant c (conjectured; best known is D(f) = O(rank(M_f))
exp: Log-rank conjecture: D(f) = O(log^c rank(M_f)). Lower bound: D(f) ≥ log rank(M_f) (Mehlhorn-Schmidt). Upper bound: D(f) ≤ rank(M_f) (trivial). The conjecture is that D and log rank are polynomially related. Best known: D(f) = O(√rank · log rank) (Lovett 2016).
